Flex Agg ++ — dashboard guide

Barra-style factor-risk on eleven hedge-fund 13F books · what each panel means and how to use it

Everything you see is computed by the Atoti cube and served through a small guarded API — the dashboard never invents a number. This guide covers each panel.

The book: eleven managers

The model was built on the Soros 13F book and now carries eleven: Soros plus Bridgewater, Citadel, Millennium, Renaissance, AQR, Two Sigma, D. E. Shaw, Point72, Tiger Global and Elliott. Each is a separate Book — a quarterly weight overlay from that manager's own 13F filings, on its own filing calendar. Pick one in the context bar; every number on every panel is for the book you picked. The factor model itself is shared: one cross-section, one set of factor returns, eleven books priced against it.

Four things to know before you read a number for a manager other than Soros.

  • ETFs and trusts are dropped. A cross-sectional style loading on a diversified fund is meaningless, so index / commodity / crypto vehicles are filtered out of every filing. The share dropped is disclosed per book, not absorbed: Bridgewater 24.5% of its 13F by value, Millennium 11.6%, Citadel 6.8%, Soros 1.9%. Read Bridgewater's book as a small equity slice of its real macro book — most of what it runs never appears in a 13F at all.
  • The desk limits are still calibrated for Soros. Thresholds are not per-book yet, so a RAG status on another manager compares that book to Soros's tolerances. /limits says so in its response (calibrated_for, cross_book_thresholds).
  • Four panels are Soros-only. Estimation universe (membership, funnel, span), style drift and PnL attribution read precomputed artifacts built for one book. Ask for another and they return a clear book_mismatch rather than serving Soros's numbers under the wrong name.
  • Attribution measures are off in the grid while more than one book is loaded — they're baked without a book key, so a name two managers both hold would read one arbitrary manager's weight. The pivot rejects them outright and points at the per-book precompute instead.
Where the books come from

SEC EDGAR 13F-HR information tables, one CIK per manager (Elliott stitches two — the current entity and its predecessor). History bottoms out at 2013-06-30 for every manager: earlier 13F-HRs are plain text with no machine-readable table. The model's sample starts 2016.

Two UIs, the same numbers

There are two front-ends, both pure clients of the same API — no number is computed differently between them.

  • flexagg2++ (the Vite app) is the current UI. A left rail of lenses, one job each: Overview · Pivot · Trends · Stress · What-if · Universe · Drift · Attribution · Changes · Model · Checks · Ask. A context bar across the top sets book, date and scenario set for every lens at once.
  • flexagg++ (the older Streamlit app) is still served during the transition, with two pages — Overview and Pivot — and the whole-book panels as drill-downs under Overview.

This guide is organised by panel, so it reads against either. Where the two differ it says so. The panel-to-lens mapping is mostly one-to-one: each section below is its own lens in flexagg2++, and a drill-down under Overview in Streamlit.

Overview is the landing page in both: a scorecard of the book's key risk numbers (Scenario VaR 99, Expected shortfall, factor/specific split, Top-5 risk share, net/gross), each with a sparkline of its trend; a red/amber/green strip for limits / data quality / backtest / reconcile; and the top risk contributions (CTV) with net exposures as the secondary read.

Two panels are Streamlit-only

Drawdown and Liquidity were cut from the Vite rail in the 2026-07-02 scope review, along with the "Risk by level" attribution tab and the Basel-zone display. The endpoints still serve and are still tested — the panels just aren't on the new UI. Both are documented below.

Overview — status strips

🚦 Desk limits (RAG)

A red/amber/green read of the book against the desk limit set, shown on every view. It's book-level and independent of the pivot you're looking at.

  • green within limits · amber past the warn threshold · breach past the hard limit.
  • Checks: Scenario VaR 99, Scenario ES 97.5 (book-level, read against one scenario set) and Top-5 risk share, plus single-name and sector weight concentration. The limits sit on the two Kupiec-backtested scenario metrics; the house Total VaR 99 composite is kept as a measure but is legacy, and model vol σ = √(x′Fx + w′Δw) is the desk's reference risk number.
  • All limits are upper bounds. Expand Limit detail for value vs warn vs cap and the offending name/sector.
Edit the limits

Edit limits.json at the repo root — reloaded on every check, no restart. The VaR/ES limits read against the scenario set in scenario_set (default HistFull); Top-5 risk share is full-history and scenario-set independent. The thresholds are calibrated for the Soros book — calibrated_for in the file, echoed by the API, and flagged when you read another manager against them.

🔎 Data quality

A pass/warn/fail trust check on the exact frames the cube is serving — key integrity, referential integrity, value ranges, calendar continuity, coverage. Expand for every check plus the known stubs: the demo universe is capped, Country is stubbed to "US" for all names, and a handful of names carry an "Unknown" sector. Read the risk numbers with those caveats in mind.

📊 VaR backtest (model validation)

Does the VaR actually hold up? At 99%, losses should beat VaR on ~1% of days. The backtest counts how often that happened over history, runs the Kupiec POF test, and assigns the Basel traffic-light zone.

  • The 13F book has no live daily P&L, so this is a constant-portfolio backtest: today's book applied to the daily factor-return history, rolling a window to estimate VaR each day. It validates the methodology, not a trading record.
  • The default estimator is FHS (filtered historical simulation, λ=0.94) — chosen by a sweep because it lands ~1.0% breaches (green) where plain historical sim under-covers and a normal EWMA over-breaches on the fat tail.
methodwhat it does
fhs (default)EWMA-vol-scaled empirical tail — reactive and fat-tailed
equalplain rolling historical simulation (equal-weighted window)
ewmaRiskMetrics parametric-normal (reactive but thin-tailed)

📈 Risk trends (2016–2024)

Risk over time, not just today: Scenario VaR 99 & ES 97.5, Risk HHI (1 / HHI ≈ the effective number of independent bets), and the top style-factor exposures. Pick the scenario set; answers "is risk rising, and where is it coming from?"

🧪 Stress test (custom & reverse)

Two modes. Custom shock — set any per-factor move in σ (standard deviations) and see the book P&L, with a per-factor contribution breakdown (P&L = Σ exposure × (σ × factor vol), the same engine as the built-in Hypo scenarios). Reverse stress — give a target loss and get, per factor, the single-factor move that would breach it, ranked by |σ| so the book's most vulnerable factor is on top (for this long-equity book that's the Market factor — it has unit beta, so it takes the smallest move).

🔀 Pre-trade / what-if

Edit the weight of any holding (0 = drop), or add a name from the coverage universe (the "add from coverage universe" picker lists every name with loadings that isn't currently held), then run. You see the book risk impact before vs after — Scenario VaR / ES, Total VaR, Specific vol, Top-5 risk share, and gross/net. Risk is recomputed from the same loadings, factor returns and specific variance the cube uses, so the "before" column matches the cube's reported numbers and the Δ column is the trade's effect. Trim a concentrated name and watch the Top-5 share fall; double one and watch it rise. The panel also discloses unpriced held names — names with no loadings that date, outside free-data coverage — so holdings plus unpriced always recover the full 13F weight.

📉 Drawdown

The path lens VaR and ES miss. The current book is applied to the scenario set's daily factor-return history and compounded into a constant-portfolio equity curve; the panel charts that curve and the underwater (peak-to-trough) area, with the max drawdown, the peak→trough dates and the recovery. On the Soros book over full history this reads ≈ −39% — the Feb–Mar 2020 COVID crash — a path risk a single-day VaR can't show. Meaningful on long paths (HistFull, event sets); a one-shock Hypo set is too short.

💰 PnL attribution (realized, factor + residual)

Where the money actually came from. The book's realized return (price-only, drifting buy-and-hold weights between 13F filings) is split into a factor-explained part and a residual — they sum exactly, because the residual is the model's own regression residual. Three tabs: Attribution — the cumulative Market / Style / Specific chart with the realized line, the by-factor table (average exposure, factor return, Carino-linked contribution, t-stat) and the coverage disclosure, over a selectable period (trailing 12m default). Residual diagnostics — is the residual large (information ratio, realized vs predicted specific vol) and is it correlated (lag-1/2 autocorrelation, a regression on the factor returns, the Barra bias statistics), each with a plain green/amber/red verdict; uncorrelated and well-sized = genuine diversified stock-picking. Risk ↔ PnL reconcile — each factor's realized contribution read against the band its start-of-period risk implied, base and stressed (vols up, correlations toward 1); a dot outside even the stressed band is a risk the decomposition missed — investigate, gain or loss alike. The same attribution drills factor→name in the pivot via the Factor contribution / Specific PnL / Realized PnL measures (the value at a month reads as the PnL over the following month — the month those exposures explain).

💧 Liquidity (days-to-liquidate)

How long to unwind the book. Each name's days-to-liquidate = market value ÷ (participation × ADV), where ADV is its trailing-63-day dollar volume and participation is the share of ADV you'll trade per day (slider, default 20%). The panel shows the share of the book you can exit within a horizon (slider, default 5 days), the weighted-average days, the least-liquid names, and any name with no ADV (delisted / illiquid — reported separately, never counted as instant). On the Soros book at 20% participation ~87% of weight clears within 5 days, weighted-average ≈ 2.2 days, worst ≈ 13 days.

📋 What changed (quarter-over-quarter)

A deterministic diff between this 13F filing and the prior one. Three reads: positions entered / exited / resized by weight; factor-exposure drift attributed to its sources (rotation from names entering/exiting vs re-pricing from held-name loading drift — the same split as the style-drift panel); and the book risk delta (Scenario VaR / ES, Total VaR, Top-5 risk share, specific vol, gross/net) computed at each date with the what-if math, so it's cube-consistent. An on-demand button writes a grounded "what changed" read that leads with the biggest move and flags drift as intentional (rotation) vs not (loading drift).

Estimation-universe diagnostics

A four-phase read of the universe the model is built on and where the book sits relative to it — from Chris's (Soros risk) review. The first three live in one 🌐 Estimation universe panel; the fourth is its own.

🌐 Estimation universe — membership, funnel, span

  • Index membership (point-in-time). For each 13F filing, the book's weight split across S&P 500 (read as-of the filing date, survivorship-free) / S&P 400–600 / outside the S&P 1500 / unclassified. Answers "does the book reach names a clean large-cap universe wouldn't cover?" — on the latest filing ~20% sits outside the S&P 1500.
  • Filtration funnel. The point-in-time S&P 500 run through a documented data-quality filter stack (size, history, trading frequency, liquidity/ADV, completeness, stability buffer), tagging the first filter that drops each name. Near-flat by design — the S&P 500 is already committee-curated, so the filters confirm clean data rather than carve much away.
  • Span / high-confidence check. Is each holding inside the factor-space the estimation universe spans (high confidence) or out beyond it (extrapolation)? Measured by Mahalanobis distance from the estimation cloud, with a 2D factor-pair scatter (cloud vs book) and a per-name verdict. ~82% of the Soros book sits inside on average, drifting out since 2021.

🧭 Style-drift attribution (intentional vs not)

The Soros book drifted out of the S&P 500's factor space since ~2021 (into smaller, higher-vol names). Was that intentional (a deliberate tilt / new PM) or unintentional (risk re-pricing)? The panel tracks the book's net factor exposure over time and decomposes each factor's drift into rotation (new names entering / exiting) vs held-name loading drift. Rotation-dominated leans intentional → update the benchmark; loading-drift-dominated leans unintentional → update the hedge. On this book the post-2021 drift is rotation-dominated, so it leans intentional. The final call needs desk knowledge (the manager's intent); the panel lays out the evidence.

Risk-analyst commentary (per view)

Under any grid view, the 🔍 Risk-analyst commentary button writes a short risk-manager read of exactly the numbers on screen.

  • It re-runs the same guarded query the grid shows, then sends only those figures to the model. It is the plain Messages API with no tools — the model has zero access to the cube, the filesystem, or anything else, and cannot re-query.
  • It's grounded: cite the numbers, invent nothing, and lead with any limit breach.
  • On-demand only (no spend unless clicked); cached per view + slice. Try it on the saved views under Public / Soros 13F filings.

💬 Ask the risk model (scoped Q&A)

Ask a free-text question and the model answers from the live cube. Unlike the per-view commentary, this one has a tool — but exactly one: query_cube, the same guarded pivot the grid uses. So it pulls its own slices to answer, citing the numbers it queried (each query is shown inline), and can reach nothing else — no off-allowlist measure, no filesystem, no web, no second tool. The loop is bounded, so it pulls a few slices and answers. Example: "Which factor drives the most Total VaR on HistFull at the latest date?" → it queries Total VaR by factor for that date and set, then reports that Market is ~97% (the uniform unit market loading) with the style factors a rump.

The pivot

The main grid is a generic pivot over the cube: put dimensions on Rows/Columns, pick Measures, slice with the Slicers. Every number — including totals — is computed by the cube (totals are recomputed at the aggregated level, never summed from cells, because VaR is non-additive). Save a configuration as a view from the Repository panel.

Flex Agg ++ · factor-risk proof-of-concept on free/public data. All figures are model output on a capped demo universe — not investment advice.
